newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: UN's Annan welcomes Wiesenthal support on mines.
newsitem.headline: UN's Annan welcomes Wiesenthal support on mines.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan met veteran Nazi hunter Simon Wiesenthal on Monday and welcomed his offer to support a U.N. drive to ban all land mines across the globe, U.N. officials said.

"The secretary-general welcomed Wiesenthal's initiative to lend his name and support for the U.N.'s campaign to ban landmines," U.N. spokeswoman Nancy Borman told Reuters after the two men met for half an hour in a Vienna hotel.
"He assured Wiesenthal the U.N. was doing a lot in this area and that clearing up existing fields was a top priority," she added.

Over 100 million land mines lie buried in 64 countries around the world. According to U.N. statistics, land mines kill or maim a person every 20 minutes, or 25,000 people a year, including many children.
Wiesenthal, 88, appeared briefly before journalists and said he had discussed land mines with Annan, who is on a three-day visit to Vienna, home to several U.N. organisations.
Wiesenthal, who says he helped to bring hundreds of escaped Nazis to book in the past 50 years, is a survivor of the Holocaust and has been active in human rights issues on behalf of the U.N.
A U.N. official said Wiesenthal wanted Annan's blessing before embarking on his plans to back the land mine ban.
One of his first projects will be to visit the Jewish cemetery in Sarajevo to try to win support for a speedy de-mining of the area, the official said.

"The U.N. should again urge its member countries and their governments to cease the production of land-mines and cut off the sale of existing stocks," Wiesenthal said in a statement from the Vienna Jewish Documentation Centre which he heads.
Countries should follow the example of Austria, which imposed a ban on land mines in December 1996, he said.
The so-called "Ottawa Process", led by Canada and involving 50 nations, aims to achieve a ban on the production, stockpiling, export and use of land mines by December.
Wiesenthal called for countries where mines are located to prepare maps of mined areas to enable de-mining operations under the auspices of the U.N.
Minefields must be closed off and protective measures set up to prevent children from straying on to them, he added.
